display_title: Agent Tuning in a Shared-Market Simulation: Holdout-Gated Search and Sim-to-Real Validation
one_liner: A heuristic agent for a two-player farming simulation with a shared, finite market, tuned by holdout-gated search and checked against a live ladder.
problem: Kaggle Kaggriculture: manage a farm for 720 turns against one opponent. Both players sell into the same finite market, so each player's sales lower the other's prices. The task is a Cournot-style competitive allocation problem, not single-agent optimisation.
approach: A hand-built policy with a GA and grid search over its constants. Candidates are graded on a deterministic hash-based search/holdout split of recorded ladder episodes, both in-band and out-of-band, then in closed-loop head-to-head. The engine version is pinned and verified by coin-exact replay reconstruction.
decision_relevance: Shows habits that transfer to combat-model and wargame analysis: verifying the simulator against ground truth before trusting it, keeping holdouts when many candidates are tried, measuring the sim-to-real gap, and noticing when the search space excludes the optimum.

headline_results.claim: v36 beat the previous agent v32 65-15 in 80 closed-loop head-to-head games (about 81%, 95% CI about 71-88%)
The best SELL_THRESHOLD values form a plateau (0.02-0.15) that lay entirely below the GA's search floor of 0.20, so the search could never have found them
Sweeping 154 values across 48 never-searched constants (~48k games) produced no improvement; the top candidates collapsed on holdout and head-to-head
The engine version matters: 24/24 rated replays reconstruct coin-exact on kaggle-environments 1.32.5 vs 22/24 on 1.32.4

limitations: The out-of-band gate replays recorded opponent actions open-loop, so opponents do not react to the agent
Band confound: top-band agents contest the shared market with different opponents, which distorts absolute margins
One holdout split is reused across many candidates, so selection effects are not fully controlled
The ladder is non-stationary: ratings inflate as the field grows, so rating changes over time are confounded
The top-band gate has only 6 seats
blockers_before_featuring: Public repo is 58 commits behind local: the v36 ship, holdout gates and ledger validation are not on GitHub
TUNING.md/NEXT.md headline 'PREDICTION CONFIRMED: v29 rates 1100.9' (n=15 episodes) is contradicted by v29's later ratings of 984.4 and 961.6, and was never retracted
Leaderboard rating/rank claims (1008.5; ~1,195/3,380) have no tracked evidence, and '~35th percentile' is inverted (it is the top 35%, about the 65th percentile)
No uncertainty on win counts or margins; 'better on every instrument' rests on 145 vs 143 of 152 and tied holdout wins
README is a 1,869-line lab notebook with contradictory 'current agent' sections (v29 vs v36; league 47-3 vs 70-0); plain-language explanation starts at line 907
Repo described as a 'compendium' but covers a single competition
No requirements.txt or single entry command; gate corpora are gitignored, so gates cannot be rerun from a clone; ~65 tracked replay JSONs (~1.5 GB) and 53 near-duplicate main*.py files
